notes.title: How we made Velvet 89? A look at our developer tools.
notes.content:
Hi!
First of all, thanks so much for playing Velvet 89, with 45 000+ of your it makes our developer hearts very happy. Secondly: tools! Velvet 89 was a first hidden object game for us, which meant we had to adapt and come up with new software solutions to the issues such as "create a huge crowd, but make sure its diverse and ensure that there are not two target characters". 

Hence, this post, where I’ll show you some of the special tweaks our very own Tereza made to Unity engine to make our life way easier. We will look a bit under the hood, but if you have any other questions, leave them below and I’ll get back to you.

[h1]Character setup[/h1]
The most important thing: our protesters! Each of them is composed of various interchangeable parts: heads, torsos, legs, hairs, glasses, signs or flags. Ondřej Javora drew them, put them together in Adobe After Effects and then imported into Unity. Tereza then made this menu that enabled us to quickly iterate different versions of each character type, experiment with different parts and let the engine generate many variations quickly, without us needing to assemble them by hand.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145708/ac09cd3f39cfd380d803aa3720a99ab7c3d0902a.gif[/img]

[h1]Crowd generator[/h1]
With the characters set, our squares and streets needed populating! Hence, the crowd generation tool. First, we created what we call "Figure Bundle", a list of characters needed for a particular scene. The tool Tereza made also enabled us to set how often each of them should appear. And then, we could generate our crowds! All we had to do was to set the amount of people in the scene (hundreds in Teplice, thousands and thousands in Letná/Ostrava), how spread the crowd should be and how tightly packed protesters should be.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145708/b0d946f3a0ed3a607830b427e6f3818db2ce0c42.gif[/img]

[h1]Figure brush[/h1]
But we could not leave everything on the computer as we wanted to polish each scene the best we could. To that end, we got "Figure Brush" to quickly draw handpicked selections of characters and delete them, refining the crowd to our liking.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145708/1e393e6eddcab8424eea68f572e9a6a4b64fcf6e.gif[/img]

[h1]Similarities finder[/h1]
To ensure we did not have any baffling doubles of our target characters (then ones you are tasked with finding), Tereza made a special tool to help us. Either to spot those exactly the same characters as the target ones or those that are very similar: we did not want to make players hunt for almost the same doorman with only difference being a small hat. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145708/8dd0399d57c9e86e9b2bf5be375835e8e4323860.gif[/img]

There is of course a lot of smaller things happening under the hood (layering, hints, animations and much more), but these are the big ones that made Velvet 89 happen.

I hope this was an interesting foray into how the game was made! Thanks for playing and all the feedback you’ve been giving us and let us know, if you’d like to see another hidden object game by Charles Games in the future or [i]perhaps[/i] an expansion to Velvet 89. Who knows!

Have a great day,
Ondřej
Charles Games

notes.title: Velvet 89 is a free hidden object game that tells the story of the 1989 Czechoslovakian revolution
notes.content:
Velvet 89 is a free hidden object game that tells the story of communist Czechoslovakia's "Velvet Revolution" in 1989, which brought an end to 41 years of one-party rule and led to the founding of a parliamentary republic. The game released earlier this month, and you can find it on Steam, iOS and Android. I know nothing about the Velvet Revolution, but I do have some quick thoughts on the use of a format I associate with Where's Wally to capture a process of extraordinary political change.

Read more

notes.title: Velvet 89 is released!
notes.content:
Hello and happy Velvet 89 release day!

We are so happy to finally show you the game we’ve been working on so hard. Five protests in four cities with 50 stories await you and your hidden object finding skills. Thanks for being interested in Velvet 89 and we hope you’ll enjoy the game!

And if you do, leave a review, because it helps us a lot as Steam shows the game to more players, spreading the historical events we recreated and important stories we tell.

In any case, let us know how you like the game. 

Happy playing!

Ondřej

notes.title: Preview: three new protests
notes.content:
Hi! 
With Velvet 89 right around the corner (October 17th, everyone!), we felt we might as well show you some birds-eye views of the protests you’ll encounter in game.

For this batch, we selected three of them, each important to how Velvet Revolution played out. Keep in mind these are pre-final so some changes might occur.


[h2]Národní street, Prague[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145708/4cf6ebadeaa92138d664f682333ce76b3f446b95.jpg[/img]
The pivotal moment of the Velvet Revolution, a scene depicting mere moments before regime police attacked and brutally beaten the peaceful protesters. In the game, you’ll learn more about the motivations of those who came to the demonstration.

[h2]České budějovice[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145708/10cdd6810512cace5ab874243a14c24922dc0740.jpg[/img]
We wanted to show how the revolution spread into regions, so on the main square of this south bohemian city, you’ll encounter both those who are very much pro democracy, as well as those who are more cautious. 

[h2]Letná, Prague[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145708/fd62e89ace32779bbbf9b76bd165731900d20c35.jpg[/img]
And finally, Letná in Prague! The biggest demonstration (more than 800 000 in real life!), a clear sign that times are about to change and that the general strike is about to happen. 

If you feel like these are big, then do not worry. We have a handy hint system in place to help you if you get lost and these are zoomed-out views of the scenes. In the game (that releases on October 17th, yay!), you’ll be much closer to the ground, able to spot all the differences between our characters much more easily.

So that’s it for today’s preview! We are so much looking forward to showing you the whole thing. 

Spread the word and let us know what you’ll looking forward the most in Velvet 89 :)

Have a great day,
Ondřej
Charles Games

notes.title: First level, first look: Teplice
notes.content:
Hi! We can’t wait to show you the full game, but for now, a sneak peek of the first level will have to do. It is a level set in northern Bohemian city of Teplice – where in 1989 an environmental protest began, suddenly and quickly turning into anti-regime demonstrations. 

It is an often-overlooked chapter of the Velvet Revolution and we hope our game can shed at least a little light onto it. Check the outline of the level at:
[previewyoutube=LxZhlW-0kSo;full][/previewyoutube]

If this sparked your interest, you can learn more about these protests on the [url=https://english.radio.cz/25-years-environmental-protests-preceded-velvet-revolution-8278194#:~:text=The%20Velvet%20Revolution%20which%20toppled,student%20decided%20enough%20was%20enough.]Czech Radio website[/url].

Also, if you like our game, consider sharing a word.

Until next time,
Ondřej
Charles Games
